name: NVIDIA DGX-1 (8x Tesla V100 32GB SXM2, NVLink)
architecture: Volta (8x Tesla V100 32GB SXM2 on NVLink plane)
memory_bandwidth_basis: per-GPU ~900 GB/s HBM2; ~7.2 TB/s aggregate but TP decode is bound by per-GPU bandwidth
notes: Complete used DGX-1 / clone (Inspur NF5488M5, Supermicro SYS-4028/4029) with 8x V100-32GB SXM2 = 256 GB HBM2 total. Asking prices $3,000-6,000; the r/homelab $2,500 find is the realistic cheap band. ~3-3.5 kW PSU and 200+ dB rack fan noise - garage/rack only. Volta has no FP8/INT4 tensor cores and FlashAttention-2 does not target Volta, so GPTQ/AWQ via vLLM or text-generation-inference is the practical path. Estimated 30-50 tok/s on 70B Q4-class across the NVLink plane (see comm-dgx1-8x-v100-llama33-70b-q4-decode-est) - highest tok/s/$ in the big-memory guide if you can tolerate power, noise and Volta-era software archaeology.
